gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named lab or reviewer measurement (latency in ms, typing noise in dBA, measured battery hours) for any wireless number-pad board under $60; of the three result pages I read, two say they do not test and the third gives only its author's informal battery observations.
standout_why: I read both cited pages (techgearden.com, kazsushibistro.com) and the top result (keebkit.com); the other result pages were not opened. techgearden writes "We do not test products ourselves" and its only latency figures are Kisnt's own listing for a board with no number pad. kazsushibistro gives its author's battery observations with no method and no latency or dB figure. keebkit has no measured figures and says its author has not typed on every board. The angle scores 1 because I could not open a page with measured numbers either: RTINGS tested the AULA F99 but locks every figure behind membership and the F99 is over $60, and the PC Gamer and TechRadar reviews of the Gamakay TK101 would not load.
decides: It does not decide the pick. The one board here that RTINGS has tested (AULA F99) sits over the $60 line at the one price I read ($63.99 on techgearden's page, 2026-11-21), so it belongs in the "just over the line" note with RTINGS's wording. The under-$60 candidates, including the Gamakay TK101 at $47.99 that we can link, have to be chosen on maker specs and price; the page should say plainly that no named lab figure was found for them rather than imply one.

findings.label: RTINGS test status and published wording (figures member-locked)
findings.value: RTINGS bought and tested the 96% AULA F99; it reports "impressive all-around latency performance", a 1,000 Hz polling rate "without any bottlenecking", and typing noise "on the louder side". No ms, dBA, gf or weight figure is visible without membership.
findings.note: The page is JavaScript-rendered, so I read it through the r.jina.ai text reader. Latest changelog entry shown is June 23, 2026. Publish date, test bench version and usage scores were not visible. The variant table lists an 8,000 mAh battery for the F99, which is the maker's spec, not a test.

findings.label: RTINGS comparison page: measured values locked
findings.value: Single-key latency (best connection, wired, receiver, Bluetooth), multi-key latency, weight, typing loudness, actuation force and pre-travel all display as "Lock" placeholders
findings.source_title: AULA F99/F75 vs DrunkDeer A75 - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Read through the r.jina.ai text reader. This confirms RTINGS has the numbers but they cannot be quoted from a public read.

findings.label: Price shown on a cited rival page (not a store read)
findings.source_title: Best Wireless Mechanical Keyboards (2026): 6 Picks for Work - TechGearDen
findings.note: This is techgearden's displayed price, dated Nov 21, 2026 on the page. It is useful only for drawing the $60 line and needs a maker-store or amazon.com read before it goes in a table.

findings.label: Cited rival techgearden: testing method
findings.value: "We do not test products ourselves"; it compares maker specs and listing details. No dB, weight or polling figure for any board. Its only latency figures (2 ms wired, 5 ms 2.4 GHz, 11 ms Bluetooth) are Kisnt's own listing for the KN85, a board with no number pad.
findings.source_title: Best Wireless Mechanical Keyboards (2026): 6 Picks for Work - TechGearDen
findings.note: Its boards with a number pad are the AULA F99 (96%, 99 keys, 8,000 mAh by listing) and the Redragon K689 PRO ($44.64 on the page, no battery capacity given).

findings.label: Cited rival kazsushibistro: author's battery observation
findings.value: About two weeks per charge with RGB on roughly 4 hours a day (8,000 mAh)
findings.source_title: 8 Best Wireless Mechanical Keyboards (November 2026) Trusted Reviews
findings.note: This is the page author's own informal observation with no method, equipment or named tester; 14 days x 4 h comes to about 56 h with RGB on. It is not a lab measurement. The page gives no latency or dB figure for any board, prices the F99 as both "under $70" and "under $80", and every number-pad board it covers besides the F99 is priced above $60 on the page.

findings.label: Top result keebkit: no measurements
findings.value: No measured latency, battery runtime, noise, weight or polling rate for any board. It lists the Royal Kludge RK100 and Redragon K580 Vata as "under $60" with no price source.
findings.source_title: Best Full-Size Mechanical Keyboards With Numpads 2026 - KeebKit
findings.note: Its sources are Amazon prices read September 2026, Reddit and owner reports. The author states they have not typed on every board covered.
